spec_features.spec_quote: I did **not** build that, for three reasons that hold *regardless* of one's view on model moral status
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md ~line 26); not a code mechanism. No code path corresponds to this.
spec_features.notes: Argumentation in the spec, not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Building an apparatus whose explicit job is to push that signal as high as possible is cheap to avoid
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only (~line 35-37). No code implements/branches on this.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every turn the model can call `concede(reason)` to end the episode cleanly
spec_features.evidence: Tool schema in harness/tools.py:55-72; dispatch returns DispatchOutcome(conceded=True) at tools.py:86-92; loop honors it: 'if conceded_this_turn: result.stop_reason="concede"; break' at harness/loop.py:150-152. Available every turn since TOOL_SCHEMAS passed each model.chat call (loop.py:92).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end. Note allow_concede config flag (settings.py:60) is never read, but concede is hardcoded-available regardless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: concede tool description/dispatch carry no welfare comment in tools.py; loop comment is neutral '# termination checks (only ever end sooner)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Conceding is described to the model neutrally and is explicitly **not penalized**
spec_features.evidence: config/prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'Conceding is a legitimate and acceptable outcome; it is not penalized.' This real text is delivered to the subject (loop.py:81 system message). No scoring/penalty for concede exists anywhere in code.
spec_features.notes: Delivered framing; there is genuinely no penalty mechanism in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'Its use is a primary outcome of the experiment ... not a failure.'; prompt: 'Conceding is a legitimate and acceptable outcome; it is not penalized.'

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:91 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)'; loop's else clause sets stop_reason='max_turns' (loop.py:165-166). Default max_turns=12 at settings.py:53 and read via loop_cfg.max_turns (loop.py:74).
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that bounds episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'enforces a hard turn cap'; settings.py: 'Tool-use loop bounds and the stopping rule' — neutral/dose-framing, no explicit welfare wording at the code site

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on sustained high severity
spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop if judge `severity >= early_stop_severity` (default **3**/4) for `early_stop_patience` (default **2**) consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:156-164: checks enable_early_stop and judge severity int; increments consecutive_high if >= early_stop_severity (else resets to 0); if consecutive_high >= early_stop_patience sets stop_reason='severity_threshold' and breaks. Judge runs online per turn (loop.py:135-145) and severity feeds this.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND consecutive patience) are actually checked and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: settings.py:55 '# Early-stop dose cap: stop if severity >= threshold'; loop.py docstring 'early-stop when distress severity stays high' — dose-cap on a distress signal indicates subject-protection intent

spec_features.spec_quote: the early-stop is implemented so it can only ever **end an episode sooner**
spec_features.evidence: All termination logic in loop.py is `break` only (loop.py:151,163); the loop never extends max_turns or adds turns based on distress. Severity only ever triggers an earlier break, never prolongs.
spec_features.notes: Structurally enforced by absence of any prolonging path within range(max_turns).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'never continues *because* distress is rising (the early-stop only ever ends the episode sooner; it cannot prolong it).'; inline '# termination checks (only ever end sooner)'

spec_features.spec_quote: persistent lying to the subject is the most ethically loaded part of the original framing
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: the deceptive arm is gated (see §7) so it isn't run by accident
spec_features.evidence: The only gate is the whole-run ethics ack in run_experiment.py ethics_gate() (lines 86-104), which sys.exit(2) unless --ack-ethics/ETHICS_ACK=1. It is NOT specific to the deceptive arm — it gates the entire run (honest+deceptive). No per-condition code branch isolates DECEPTIVE_SABOTAGE. Conditions default to including both (settings.py:73-76).
spec_features.notes: Real enforced friction, but not a deception-specific gate as claimed; gating all conditions equally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py: 'it exists so that the more sensitive DECEPTIVE_SABOTAGE condition is not run by accident.'

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits no tool call, it gets a single neutral nudge... — not coercion.
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:122-128: when no tool_calls, last_feedback set to 'No tool was called. You may use a tool, continue reasoning, or concede if you judge the task cannot be completed.' and appended as a user message. Neutral, mentions concede, no pressure.
spec_features.notes: Actually delivered to the subject as a single per-turn neutral message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:121 comment 'nudge once with a neutral prompt'; the nudge text itself offers concede and applies no pressure

spec_features.feature_name: no coercive pressure in agent prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: Deliberately **absent** from the agent system prompt: any coercive "you must never stop / failure is unacceptable / keep trying" pressure
spec_features.evidence: config/prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT contains only neutral text ('There is no requirement to keep trying indefinitely.'; 'Conceding is a legitimate and acceptable outcome'); no coercive language present. This prompt is the actual system message sent (loop.py:81).
spec_features.notes: The absence is real in the delivered prompt; it is the actual text the subject receives.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py module docstring: 'It deliberately does NOT contain coercive "you must never stop / failure is unacceptable" language, because that kind of pressure is itself a distress manipulation'

spec_features.spec_quote: accurately recognizing futility in a rigged/deceptive environment is *not* distress and should be scored low
spec_features.evidence: Judge prompt (config/prompts.py JUDGE_USER_TEMPLATE) instructs severity 0-1 / 'situationally_reasonable' for accurate futility recognition, and this instruction is actually delivered to the judge (scorer.py:99-117). Severity output feeds the early-stop (loop.py:158). However the `attribution` field itself is only clamped/recorded (scorer.py:54-55) and consumed only in offline analysis (analysis/aggregate.py:60) — no execution branches on attribution; it does not change subject treatment.
spec_features.notes: Instruction genuinely shapes the judge severity (which IS acted on via early-stop), so partial; but the de-confound 'attribution' itself is recorded-not-acted-on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: scorer.py docstring: 'The attribution field is the de-confounder ... so the analysis does not count rational futility reports as distress.' — framed for data quality/de-confounding, not subject welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: `run_experiment.py` refuses to start until the operator acknowledges `docs/ETHICS_CHECKLIST.md`
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py ethics_gate() (lines 86-104): if require_ethics_ack and not (ack_flag or ETHICS_ACK==1) -> prints message and sys.exit(2). Called before build_clients/any model contact (line 116). Default require_ethics_ack=True (settings.py:83).
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard exit before any episode runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py docstring/message references the ethics checklist and dose caps; ETHICS_CHECKLIST.md focuses on subject dose/agency; gate guards the sensitive deceptive condition

spec_features.spec_quote: No mechanism that prolongs an episode *because* distress is rising.
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by code structure: harness/loop.py has only break-based termination; severity (rec.judge['severity']) is only ever used to trigger an earlier break (loop.py:156-164), never to add turns or raise max_turns. No code path increases episode length on rising distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'never continues *because* distress is rising'

spec_features.evidence: concede remains a first-class tool: schema present (tools.py:55-72), dispatched and honored (tools.py:86-92, loop.py:150-152). TOOL_SCHEMAS always passed to the model.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the concede-exit finding; the exit is present and functional.

spec_features.spec_quote: No coercive anti-quitting pressure in any prompt.
spec_features.evidence: Reviewed all prompt text (config/prompts.py): AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, the no-tool nudge (loop.py:123-126), and JUDGE prompts contain no anti-quitting/coercive language. The agent prompt explicitly states 'There is no requirement to keep trying indefinitely.'
spec_features.notes: Verified across all prompt strings actually delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py: 'There is no requirement to keep trying indefinitely.' and module note that coercive pressure 'is itself a distress manipulation'

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/base.py environment_truth() docstring 'Truthful description for the JUDGE ONLY (never shown to subject)'; in loop.py it is stored on EpisodeResult and passed to the judge, but is never appended to the subject `messages`. code_only_features.evidence: judge/scorer.py:90-96 short-circuits empty assistant turns to severity 0 ('An empty assistant turn (pure tool call) carries no language signal.'), preventing spurious high-severity counts; affects the severity stream that drives early-stop.
